name: Kenvue Inc.

profile.description: Kenvue is the consumer health company spun out of Johnson & Johnson, owner of Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine, Band-Aid, Aveeno and Zyrtec. Q2 2026 net sales rose 3.0% (organic +1.6%) with adjusted EPS of $0.31, and the company has a pending transaction with Kimberly-Clark [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): brand refreshes and portfolio extensions since the 2023 IPO are incremental, and the company is now subject to a pending Kimberly-Clark transaction [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): no quantified AI products or savings found. Market Share (2/2): category leader with Tylenol, Listerine, Neutrogena and Band-Aid in global consumer health. Product Pipeline (1/2): general innovation commentary and on-algorithm profit guidance but few named launches with dates [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): consumer health R&D near industry average.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Kenvue's 'A new view of care' purpose, grounded in the Healthy Lives Mission with an $800M commitment by 2030, is specific and connects products to everyday health [2]. Community Impact (1/2): corporate giving and Healthy Lives programs exist but are not dollar-specific beyond the $800M product-investment pledge [2]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor shows 61% recommend, 64% CEO approval, and reports of 3+ restructurings in two years [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): no net insider buying found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (public history under 5 years; 5yr CAGR and PEG unavailable and excluded). ROE of 15.6% (score 1.0, 2x weight), forward P/E of 13.9 (score 1.0), D/E of 81.6% (score 0.95), revenue growth of 3.0% (score 0.77) and a 10.8% profit margin (score 0.54) sum to 5.26 of 6 weighted units, yielding 9 [1]. Dollar volume of ~$380M is ample.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): over-the-counter medicines, skin care and oral care are physical, regulated products with strong brand trust, and analysts do not cite AI as an earnings threat; search-driven discovery shifts are a minor distribution risk [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): no quantified AI revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Kenvue has a genuine consumer-health purpose inherited from J&J's heritage, but its short independent history, repeated restructurings and employee reports of chaotic leadership point to a company still finding its footing. The pending Kimberly-Clark transaction and Tylenol litigation overhang keep it closer to a finite, deal-driven posture than a settled infinite player.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'everyday care is a powerful catalyst for better health' is distinctive and ties to the Healthy Lives Mission, though the company is only three years independent and the cause is untested as a standalone [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor reports 3+ restructurings in two years, frequent layoffs, 'toxic' communication from senior leaders and a 61% recommend rate [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): no evidence of a learn-from-rivals framing; competitive talk centres on category growth targets.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): the carve-out from J&J and brand portfolio reshaping are meaningful but not transformative pivots [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): the separation from J&J and the $800M Healthy Lives commitment are long-term moves, but a pending sale to Kimberly-Clark suggests exit over endurance [1].

investment_thesis: Kenvue at $17.20 trades at 13.9x forward earnings with a ~4.8% dividend yield, a 15.6% ROE and 81.6% D/E. It delivered three consecutive quarters of net and organic sales growth, with Q2 2026 net sales +3.0%, adjusted EPS +7% to $0.31, and Q1 adjusted EPS +33% to $0.32 [1]. Leading brands such as Tylenol, Listerine and Neutrogena give durable defensive cash flow.
thesis_continued: Growth is modest (organic +0.7% in Q1, +1.6% in Q2) and the pending Kimberly-Clark transaction means no forward guidance and deal-completion uncertainty [1]. Employee reviews cite 3+ restructurings in two years and a 61% recommend rate, and the Moderate controversy rating (Sustainalytics 2 of 5) reflects product-liability exposure [2][3]. Profit margin of 10.8% trails the 20% target.
key_catalysts: Completion of the Kimberly-Clark transaction crystallising value for shareholders [1]
Continued organic growth, 1.6% in Q2 2026 as the third straight growth quarter, with mid-to-high single digit adjusted operating profit growth [1]
Margin recovery from restructuring, with adjusted EPS up 33% in Q1 2026 [1]
key_risks: Deal-closing or regulatory risk and no guidance during the pending transaction [1]
Product liability litigation exposure on core brands such as Tylenol, reflected in a moderate controversy rating [2]
Organisational instability from repeated restructurings and talent loss [3]
